description: Extend MooPredict to track ETFs using technical analysis and deliver actionable buy/sell/watch signals via Telegram. No manual research needed — the system tells you what to do.

target_etfs.notes: Start with these 5. Add more later once signals are stable.

phases.name: QA Fixes — Pre-requisite Before Any New Work
phases.goal: Fix the bugs identified in the current code review. These must be resolved before building new features on top of unstable foundations.

tasks.name: Fix Board Lot Fallback: 1 → 100
tasks.problem: When Futu cannot fetch the lot size for a stock, the fallback was changed from 100 to 1. HK stocks have minimum lot sizes of 100, 500, or 1000 — trading 1 share will result in failed or invalid orders on the exchange.
tasks.fix: Change the catch block fallback in get_board_lot() back to return 100, not 1. If the lot size is unknown, 100 is the safest conservative default for HK stocks.
tasks.code_change: return 1 → return 100 in the catch block of get_board_lot()

tasks.name: Fix TCP Connection Race Condition in FutuService
tasks.problem: After calling this.client.start(), the code does setTimeout(resolve, 500) to 'give the socket a moment'. This is a race condition — if the TCP handshake takes longer than 500ms, InitConnect (cmd 1001) fires on an unready socket and will fail silently or crash.
tasks.fix: Move the resolve() call inside the socket's 'connect' event callback in FutuTcpClient.start(). The promise should only resolve when the TCP connection is actually established, not after an arbitrary delay.
files_affected: server/services/futuTcpClient.ts — emit a 'ready' event or return a Promise from start()
server/services/futuService.ts — await the actual connection, not a timeout

tasks.name: Audit get_board_lot() Callers for Unhandled Throws
tasks.problem: get_board_lot() now throws an error when FutuOpenD is not connected, instead of returning 100 silently. Any caller that did not previously handle an exception will now crash the surrounding flow.
tasks.fix: Search all callers of get_board_lot() and ensure they have try/catch or fallback handling. Alternatively, restore the silent fallback behavior and throw only in contexts where the error is meaningful.
tasks.action: Run: grep -rn 'get_board_lot' server/ to find all call sites

tasks.name: Add Confirmation Guard to /api/system/clear-trades
tasks.problem: POST /api/system/clear-trades runs TRUNCATE positions, trade_proposals RESTART IDENTITY CASCADE with no confirmation step. One accidental POST wipes all trade history permanently. There is no soft-delete, no backup, no recovery.
tasks.fix: Require a ?confirm=true query parameter before executing the TRUNCATE. If the param is missing, return a 400 with a warning message explaining what will be deleted. Example: if (!req.query.confirm) return res.status(400).json({ error: 'Add ?confirm=true to proceed. This will permanently delete all positions and proposals.' })

tasks.name: Re-evaluate minConfidence Drop from 0.5 to 0.3
tasks.problem: minConfidence was lowered from 0.5 to 0.3 AND the Ollama prompt was changed to 'BE AGGRESSIVE'. Combined, these changes mean significantly more low-quality opportunities will pass through to StrategyAgent and potentially trigger paper trades. Expect more noise and false positives.
tasks.fix: Monitor the number of signals generated per session in paper mode. If more than 5-10 opportunities are being generated per scrape cycle, the threshold is too low. Recommended: keep minConfidence at 0.4 as a middle ground. Revert to 0.5 if signal quality is poor after 1 week of paper trading.
tasks.action: Do not change code yet — monitor for 3-5 days of paper trading, then decide

tasks.name: Monitor Ollama Load from Doubled Scheduler Frequency
tasks.problem: Scrape schedule changed from every 2 hours to every 1 hour. Two additional opening-bell triggers were added (09:15 and 21:15). Total scrape frequency is roughly 3-4x higher than before. Each scrape cycle sends multiple batches to Ollama for analysis, which is CPU-heavy on local hardware.
tasks.fix: No immediate code change. Monitor Ollama response times and system CPU during market hours. If Ollama starts timing out or queue backs up, revert to 0 */2 * * 1-5 (every 2 hours) and remove one of the opening bell triggers.
tasks.action: Check logs after first full trading day — look for 'Ollama discovery failed' errors

phases.name: ETF Watchlist & Data Foundation
phases.goal: Teach the system what ETFs to track and pull their price data reliably.

tasks.name: Create ETF Watchlist Config
tasks.description: Add a static config file listing the ETFs to monitor, their sector, and their swing trading timeframe (short: 10-20 days, long: 50+ days). This is the source of truth for what the system watches.
details: Define ETF entries with: symbol, name, sector, market (US/HK), timeframe preference
Include context for each ETF (e.g. XLE is oil-sensitive, QQQ is tech-sensitive)
Export as a typed array so all agents can reference it

tasks.name: ETF Price Data Fetcher
tasks.description: Use yahoo-finance2 (already installed) to fetch OHLCV (Open/High/Low/Close/Volume) data for each ETF. Fetch daily candles for the past 90 days to support technical indicator calculations.
details: Function: fetchEtfData(symbol: string): returns 90-day OHLCV array
Function: fetchEtfSnapshot(symbol: string): returns current price, change %, volume
Cache results for 15 minutes to avoid rate limiting
Handle errors gracefully — if one ETF fails, continue with others

tasks.name: DB Table: etf_signals
tasks.description: Create a Postgres table to store generated signals so we don't re-alert on the same signal, and can track signal history.
details: Columns: id, symbol, signal_type (BUY/SELL/WATCH), entry_price, target_price, stop_loss, confidence, reason, timeframe, created_at, alerted_at
Unique constraint on (symbol, signal_type, DATE(created_at)) — one signal per ETF per day per type
Index on symbol + created_at for fast lookups

phases.name: Technical Analysis Engine
phases.goal: Calculate the key technical indicators that generate buy/sell signals for ETFs.
phases.notes: The 'technicalindicators' npm package is already installed — use it.

tasks.name: RSI (Relative Strength Index)
tasks.description: RSI measures if an ETF is overbought or oversold on a 0-100 scale. This is the single most useful indicator for swing trading entry/exit points.

signal_rules.BUY_SIGNAL: RSI drops below 30 (oversold) — ETF is likely to bounce up
signal_rules.SELL_SIGNAL: RSI rises above 70 (overbought) — ETF is likely to pull back
signal_rules.WATCH_SIGNAL: RSI between 40-60 — neutral, no clear signal yet

tasks.implementation: Use 14-period RSI (standard). Input: array of closing prices.

tasks.name: MACD (Moving Average Convergence Divergence)
tasks.description: MACD detects momentum shifts and trend changes. A crossover (MACD line crossing signal line) is a classic swing trade entry trigger.

signal_rules.BUY_SIGNAL: MACD line crosses ABOVE signal line (bullish crossover)
signal_rules.SELL_SIGNAL: MACD line crosses BELOW signal line (bearish crossover)
signal_rules.STRENGTH: The larger the histogram bar, the stronger the momentum

tasks.name: Moving Averages (SMA 20 / SMA 50)
tasks.description: Simple moving averages show trend direction. Price above SMA20 = short-term bullish. SMA20 above SMA50 = medium-term bullish (golden cross setup).

signal_rules.BUY_SIGNAL: Price crosses above SMA20 AND SMA20 is above SMA50
signal_rules.GOLDEN_CROSS: SMA20 crosses above SMA50 — strong medium-term buy signal
signal_rules.DEATH_CROSS: SMA20 crosses below SMA50 — strong sell/avoid signal

tasks.implementation: Compute SMA20 and SMA50 from closing prices. Compare last 2 candles to detect crossovers.

tasks.name: Volume Confirmation
tasks.description: A price move on high volume is more reliable than a move on low volume. Use volume to confirm signals — weak volume = skip the signal.

signal_rules.CONFIRM: Current volume > 1.5x the 20-day average volume — signal is confirmed
signal_rules.REJECT: Current volume < 0.8x average — signal is weak, do not alert

tasks.implementation: Compute 20-day average volume. Compare today's volume against it.

tasks.name: Signal Composer
tasks.description: Combine all indicators into a single signal decision per ETF. Require at least 2 indicators to agree before generating a BUY or SELL. One indicator alone is not enough.

scoring.BUY_threshold: 2+ indicators vote BUY = generate BUY signal
scoring.SELL_threshold: 2+ indicators vote SELL = generate SELL signal
scoring.WATCH_threshold: Mixed or 1 indicator only = generate WATCH signal

tasks.name: Entry Price, Target & Stop Loss Calculator
tasks.description: For each BUY signal, automatically calculate where to enter, what the target price is, and where to cut losses. This gives the user a complete trade plan.

formulas.entry_price: Current market price at signal time
formulas.stop_loss: Entry price minus 1x ATR (Average True Range, 14-period) — automatic risk limit
formulas.short_term_target: Entry price plus 2x ATR — for 10-20 day holds
formulas.long_term_target: Entry price plus 4x ATR — for 50+ day holds
formulas.risk_reward_ratio: Must be at least 2:1 to generate a signal (don't risk $1 to make $1)

phases.name: ETF Intel Agent
phases.goal: Build the agent that runs the analysis pipeline and persists signals to the DB.

tasks.name: EtfIntelAgent
tasks.description: New agent that loops through the ETF watchlist, fetches data, runs technical analysis, and stores new signals in the DB. Designed to run on a schedule.
details: Method: runAnalysis() — iterates all ETFs in watchlist
For each ETF: fetch price data → run technical analysis → compose signal
Before saving: check DB to see if same signal was already alerted today (dedup)
If new signal: save to etf_signals table → emit event 'etf:signal_ready'
Log all analysis results even if no signal is generated (for debugging)

tasks.name: Wire EtfIntelAgent into Scheduler
tasks.description: Add EtfIntelAgent to the existing Scheduler so it runs automatically during US and HK market hours.

schedule.pre_market_scan: 0 8 * * 1-5 — 8am HKT, before HK opens. Morning briefing.
schedule.us_pre_market_scan: 0 20 * * 1-5 — 8pm HKT, before US opens. Evening briefing.
schedule.intraday_scan: 0 10,14 * * 1-5 — Mid-session checks for new signals during HK hours

tasks.name: Wire into server.ts
tasks.description: Import EtfIntelAgent in server.ts so its event listeners register on startup. Add force-scan API endpoint for manual triggering.
endpoints: POST /api/etf/scan — manually trigger a full ETF scan (useful for testing)
GET /api/etf/signals — return all signals from the last 7 days

phases.name: Telegram Signal Delivery
phases.goal: Format and send clear, actionable Telegram messages — no jargon, just what to do.

tasks.name: ETF Signal Formatter
tasks.description: Format each signal into a clean Telegram message. Beginner-friendly language. No charts, just numbers and clear instructions.

message_templates.WATCH_signal:
👀 *ETF WATCH: {symbol}*
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
Not ready to buy yet — keep an eye on this.
📝 *Why watching:* {reason}
🔔 Will alert when signal confirms.
message_templates.morning_briefing:
🌅 *ETF MORNING BRIEFING*
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
{list_of_signals_today}

_No action needed unless you see a BUY or SELL above._

tasks.name: EtfReportAgent — Event Listener
tasks.description: Subscribe to 'etf:signal_ready' events and send the formatted Telegram message. Mark signal as alerted in DB after sending.
details: Subscribe to 'etf:signal_ready' on eventBus
Format message based on signal type (BUY/SELL/WATCH)
Send via existing sendTelegramMessage()
After successful send: UPDATE etf_signals SET alerted_at = NOW() WHERE id = signal.id
If Telegram fails: log error, mark signal for retry (do not duplicate)

tasks.name: Daily Morning Briefing
tasks.description: Every trading day morning, send a summary of all active ETF signals and positions — even if nothing changed. User always knows the current state.
details: Query etf_signals for all active BUY signals from last 7 days
Query positions for any open ETF trades
Format into one clean morning summary message
Send at 08:30 HKT for HK session, 20:30 HKT for US session

phases.name: Paper Trading Integration
phases.goal: When a BUY signal fires, automatically simulate the trade in paper mode so you can track performance without real money.
phases.notes: Uses the existing ExecutionAgent and virtual_portfolio table — minimal new code needed.

tasks.name: Connect ETF Signals to ExecutionAgent
tasks.description: When EtfIntelAgent emits a BUY signal with confidence above 70%, automatically pass it to ExecutionAgent for paper trade execution.
details: Only auto-execute signals with confidence >= 0.70
Emit 'strategy:execute_trade' event with symbol, entry_price, stop_loss, target
ExecutionAgent handles the virtual balance deduction and DB write
SELL signals: trigger ExecutionAgent to close the matching open position

tasks.name: ETF Position Monitor
tasks.description: Extend ExecutionAgent's existing monitorPositions() to handle ETF-specific exit logic using the calculated stop_loss and target_price from the signal.
details: For ETF positions: read stop_loss and target from etf_signals table
If current price hits stop_loss: auto-close and send Telegram SELL alert
If current price hits target: send Telegram alert recommending exit (do not auto-close — let user decide)
Daily P&L summary for all open ETF positions

phases.name: Backtesting & Signal Tuning
phases.goal: Verify the signals would have worked historically before trusting them with real money.

tasks.name: Historical Backtest Runner
tasks.description: Fetch 1-2 years of daily OHLCV data for each ETF and replay the technical analysis day-by-day to see how many signals were correct.
metrics_to_track: Win rate: % of BUY signals that hit target before stop loss

tasks.name: Threshold Tuning
tasks.description: Based on backtest results, adjust RSI thresholds, MACD settings, and confidence minimums to maximize win rate for ETFs specifically. ETFs behave differently from individual stocks.
tasks.notes: ETFs revert to mean more reliably than stocks. RSI 35/65 thresholds may work better than classic 30/70 for ETFs with large AUM like SPY and XLE.

recommended_build_order: Phase 0 (QA fixes) FIRST — fix bugs before building new features on top
Phase 1 → Phase 2 → Phase 3 → Phase 4 (get ETF signals flowing to Telegram)
Phase 5 (paper trading) after signals are validated for a few days
Phase 6 (backtesting) can run in parallel with Phase 4/5

dependencies.new_packages_needed: None — all dependencies already exist in package.json

success_criteria.phase_1_2_3: System generates at least one signal per ETF per week when market conditions are active
success_criteria.phase_4: Telegram receives a morning briefing every trading day with clear BUY/SELL/WATCH labels
success_criteria.phase_5: Paper portfolio tracks ETF trades automatically — P&L visible via /api/etf/signals
success_criteria.phase_6: Backtest shows at least 55% win rate with 2:1 risk/reward ratio before considering real money
